data.name: Akt/PKB
data.description: Key kinase downstream of PI3K in growth signalling; activated by PDK1 at T308 and further phosphorylated by mTORC2 at S473, which shapes which substrates it hits.
data.description_beginner: A key signaling kinase that sits downstream of PI3K. It is switched on by PI3K signaling through PDK1, with mTORC2 adding a second mark that tunes what it does. It's one of the cell's central 'growth is good, keep going' signals.

studies.title: Phosphorylation and regulation of Akt/PKB by the rictor-mTOR complex
studies.authors: Sarbassov DD et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The rictor-mTOR complex (mTORC2) directly phosphorylates Akt/PKB on Ser473, regulating cell survival.

studies.title: The phosphoinositide 3-kinase pathway
studies.authors: Cantley LC

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Review establishing PI3K as a central signaling hub controlling cell survival, metabolism, and growth downstream of growth-factor receptors and upstream of Akt and mTOR.

studies.title: TSC2 is phosphorylated and inhibited by Akt and suppresses mTOR signalling
studies.authors: Inoki K; Guan KL et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Akt directly phosphorylates and inactivates TSC2, disrupting the TSC1-TSC2 complex and releasing its inhibition of mTOR - the link between growth-factor/insulin signaling and mTORC1 activation.

studies.title: Mediation of IGF-1-induced skeletal myotube hypertrophy by PI(3)K/Akt/mTOR and PI(3)K/Akt/GSK3 pathways
studies.authors: Rommel C; Bodine SC et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Shows IGF-1 drives muscle fiber hypertrophy through Akt, via both the mTOR and GSK3 branches, in cultured myotubes, establishing mTOR as a central node for muscle growth signaling.

studies.title: Rictor, a novel binding partner of mTOR, defines a rapamycin-insensitive and raptor-independent pathway that regulates the cytoskeleton
studies.authors: Sarbassov DD; Ali SM; Kim DH; Guertin DA; Latek RR; Erdjument-Bromage H; Tempst P; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Discovery of Rictor and the SECOND mTOR complex, mTORC2. Crucially showed this complex is NOT blocked by rapamycin and does not use Raptor - it controls the cytoskeleton via PKC. This is the paper that split mTOR biology into 'two faces' at the molecular level.

studies.title: DEPTOR is an mTOR inhibitor frequently overexpressed in multiple myeloma cells and required for their survival
studies.authors: Peterson TR; Laplante M; Thoreen CC; Sancak Y; Kang SA; Kuehl WM; Gray NS; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Identified DEPTOR as a built-in brake on BOTH mTOR complexes. The twist: in some multiple myelomas DEPTOR is overexpressed, which by relieving a feedback loop actually keeps pro-survival Akt signaling ON - a neat example of how an 'inhibitor' can be co-opted by cancer.

studies.title: Prolonged rapamycin treatment inhibits mTORC2 assembly and Akt/PKB
studies.authors: Sarbassov DD; Ali SM; Sengupta S; Sheen JH; Hsu PP; Bagley AF; Markhard AL; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The molecular explanation for rapamycin's dark side. Short-term rapamycin only hits mTORC1, but LONG-term treatment also strips down mTORC2 in many cells, cutting Akt signaling. This is the mechanistic root of the insulin-resistance side effect later shown in mice (see Lamming 2012) - crucial for anyone dosing rapamycin for longevity.

studies.title: Active-site inhibitors of mTOR target rapamycin-resistant outputs of mTORC1 and mTORC2
studies.authors: Feldman ME; Apsel B; Uotila A; Loewith R; Knight ZA; Ruggero D; Shokat KM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The parallel discovery to Thoreen 2009 (same year), from the Shokat lab. Their TORKinibs (PP242, PP30) block mTOR's active site, hitting both complexes and shutting down cap-dependent translation that rapamycin misses. Together these two papers established a whole new drug class beyond rapamycin.

studies.title: PRAS40 is an insulin-regulated inhibitor of the mTORC1 protein kinase
studies.authors: Sancak Y; Thoreen CC; Peterson TR; Lindquist RA; Kang SA; Spooner E; Carr SA; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Identified PRAS40 as the missing insulin-controlled brake INSIDE mTORC1. When insulin is absent PRAS40 clamps the complex shut; insulin makes Akt phosphorylate PRAS40, releasing the brake so Rheb can fully switch mTORC1 on. Explained how hormone signals set the exact strength of mTORC1 activity.

studies.title: Ablation in mice of the mTORC components raptor, rictor, or mLST8 reveals that mTORC2 is required for signaling to Akt-FOXO and PKCalpha, but not S6K1
studies.authors: Guertin DA; Stevens DM; Thoreen CC; Burds AA; Kalaany NY; Moffat J; Brown M; Fitzgerald KJ; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The foundational genetic 'dissection' of the two complexes in living mice. Deleting Raptor was lethal early (mTORC1 essential); deleting Rictor or mLST8 selectively knocked out mTORC2 signaling to Akt and PKCalpha but spared S6K1. This cleanly assigned jobs to each complex and showed mLST8 is an mTORC2-specific requirement in mice.

studies.title: mTOR inhibition augments antitumor immune effector response by reprogramming the TP53-mutant, immune-cold HNSCC tumor microenvironment
studies.authors: Nath P; Khandelwal A; Li C; Moore-Medlin T; Vasudevan SS; Alvarez VA; Franco OE; Gutkind JS; Nathan CO

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Syngeneic mouse models of TP53-mutant HNSCC
studies.finding: In syngeneic TP53-mutant HNSCC mouse models, the mTOR inhibitor everolimus reprogrammed the immune-cold tumor microenvironment: it increased CD8+ T cell and dendritic cell infiltration, reduced Tregs and HIF-1α/VEGFA-driven MDSC recruitment, boosted TNF-α/CXCL10 chemokine signaling, and reduced PD-1/PD-L1 expression — restoring T-cell cytotoxic competence and suppressing tumor growth.

studies.title: Firefox, a protein encoded by circular RNA circPVT1, is essential for MYC-driven oncogenesis
studies.authors: Tiwari A, Paithane U, Tashiro K, Hall B, Friedlein J, Saraswat M, Saulnier O, Barbosa K, Trinh Q, Bagchi A, et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human MYC-amplified cancer cell lines; xenograft mouse models
studies.finding: A micropeptide (Firefox/FFX) encoded by the circular RNA circPVT1 stimulates AKT-mTORC1 signaling and cap-dependent translation to sustain MYC protein abundance and transcriptional output. FFX depletion reduces MYC levels and impairs tumor growth in MYC-amplified xenograft models, identifying an mTORC1-linked vulnerability in MYC-driven cancers.

studies.title: Akt promotes cell survival by phosphorylating and inhibiting a Forkhead transcription factor
studies.authors: Brunet A; Blenis J et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mammalian cell lines; primary neurons (in vitro)
studies.finding: Akt phosphorylates the Forkhead transcription factor FKHRL1 (a FOXO family member), driving its cytoplasmic retention via 14-3-3 binding and blocking Fas-ligand-driven apoptosis — the discovery that placed FOXO transcription factors downstream of Akt/PI3K survival signalling.

studies.title: Temporal coding of insulin action through multiplexing of the AKT pathway
studies.authors: Kubota H; Noguchi R; Toyoshima Y; Ozaki YI; Uda S; Watanabe K; Ogawa W; Kuroda S

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Rat hepatoma cells (Fao); pulse vs sustained insulin, time-course phosphorylation plus kinetic modelling
studies.finding: The same pathway can carry different messages in the shape of its signal over time. A short insulin pulse produced transient AKT phosphorylation and a sustained dose produced sustained AKT phosphorylation. S6K read only the transient part, G6Pase only the sustained part and GSK3-beta both. Which output responds depends on the pattern, not just the amount - the clearest cell-level case in the atlas that timing carries information in this pathway.

studies.title: In Vivo Decoding Mechanisms of the Temporal Patterns of Blood Insulin by the Insulin-AKT Pathway in the Liver
studies.authors: Kubota H; Uda S; Matsuzaki F; Yamauchi Y; Kuroda S

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Rat liver in vivo (hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp with different insulin time patterns) plus mathematical model
studies.finding: The in-vivo follow-up to KUB2012. In rat liver, all temporal patterns of blood insulin were encoded at the insulin receptor, and downstream molecules decoded them selectively through AKT: S6K read the additional (pulse-like) secretion, G6Pase the basal secretion via FoxO1, GSK3-beta all of it. Modelling tied the selectivity to network structure, sensitivity and time constants. Shows that pattern decoding is not only a cell-culture effect.

studies.title: A dynamic network model of mTOR signaling reveals TSC-independent mTORC2 regulation
studies.authors: Dalle Pezze P; Sonntag AG; Thien A; Prentzell MT; Gödel M; Fischer S; Neumann-Haefelin E; Huber TB; Baumeister R; Shanley DP; Thedieck K

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Data-driven dynamic model of the insulin-mTOR network, tested in HeLa and other cell lines
studies.finding: A time-resolved, data-fitted model of the whole core insulin-mTOR network, including the mTORC1 negative feedback loop onto PI3K. Perturbing it in silico and in cells showed that TSC1-TSC2 is not a regulator of mTORC2, directly or through the feedback loop, and that mTORC2 activation runs through a PI3K variant insensitive to that loop. One of the few places where the feedback loops in the atlas are treated as a dynamical system rather than a diagram.

studies.title: Salvianolic Acid B Enhances Motor Function Recovery after Spinal Cord Injury in Association with AKT/mTOR/HIF-1α Pathway Activation and Angiogenesis.
studies.authors: Yao J; Chen Yingfeng; Pan F; Zhang S

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Salvianolic acid B improved motor recovery, neuronal survival and angiogenesis after rat spinal cord injury in association with AKT/mTOR/HIF-1α activation; the effects were reversed by the AKT inhibitor capivasertib.

studies.title: Skeletal muscle-specific ablation of raptor, but not of rictor, causes metabolic changes and results in muscle dystrophy
studies.authors: Bentzinger CF; Rueegg MA et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In mice, muscle-specific raptor loss (not rictor) causes dystrophy, showing mTORC1 is essential for muscle homeostasis.

studies.title: mTOR inhibition induces upstream receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and activates Akt
studies.authors: O'Reilly KE; Rosen N et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Cancer cell lines + patient tumours treated with the rapamycin derivative RAD001 (everolimus)
studies.finding: mTORC1 inhibition relieves feedback and activates upstream RTK-PI3K-Akt signalling. The Akt activation was demonstrated both in cancer cell lines and in patient tumours treated with RAD001 (everolimus), so this record carries a human pharmacodynamic component, not only in-vitro data. studies.title: Dietary protein governs the role of insulin signaling in the postprandial regulation of hepatic mTORC1.
studies.authors: Kalafut KC; Cormerais Y; Cissé MY; Lapp SC; Inouye KE; Hotamışlıgil GS; Manning BD

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In liver-specific mouse genetic models, AKT-mediated TSC2 phosphorylation is the main route by which insulin induces hepatic mTORC1, but is dispensable for feeding-induced activation; postprandial mTORC1 activation instead requires dietary protein, and hepatic mTORC1 signalling is not elevated in diet-induced obesity despite impaired insulin/glucose homeostasis.

studies.title: Novel mTORC1 Booster LAPTM4A Potentiates Pathological Cardiac Hypertrophy
studies.authors: Hu Y; Li W; Hu M; Tian S; Zhou S; Liu J; Cheng X; Zhang C; Zuo Y; Zhang J; Liu D; Hu Y; Chen Y; Li X; Luo L; Yang H; Bai L; Liu H; Ferdinandy P; Chiong M; Troncoso MF; Wen J; Cai J; Zhang XJ; She ZG; Zhang X; Li H

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Rat cardiomyocytes (adenoviral overexpression/knockdown); mouse cardiomyocyte-specific AAV9 overexpression and knockout, transverse aortic constriction (TAC) model
studies.finding: Identifies LAPTM4A, a lysosomal transmembrane protein, as a novel booster of mTORC1 signaling in cardiomyocytes: LAPTM4A binds NEDD4L, driving K63-linked ubiquitination of AKT and downstream mTORC1-p70S6K/4EBP1-mediated protein synthesis, without affecting lysosomal autophagy. Cardiomyocyte-specific LAPTM4A deletion attenuated TAC-induced hypertrophy/fibrosis in mice; an FDA-approved-drug screen identified magnolol as a LAPTM4A suppressor with cardioprotective effect in vivo.

studies.title: IGF2BP3-Mediated m6A Modification of OLR1 mRNA Promotes Immune Evasion in CRC via the PI3K/AKT/mTOR Pathway
studies.authors: Chen W

studies.finding: IGF2BP3 stabilizes OLR1 via m6A RNA modification, activating PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling which suppresses CD8+ T cell anti-tumor activity and drives immune evasion in colorectal cancer.

evidence.label: Animal model

studies.finding: LncRNA DLX6-AS1 activates PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling to promote necroptosis in myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury; inhibiting DLX6-AS1 suppresses necroptosis and protects cardiomyocytes.

studies.title: An ANGPTL8-AKT2-mTOR Axis Drives Adipose Senescence and Aging-Related Functional Decline
studies.authors: He Y; Pan L; Ping W; Meng C; Meng X; Guo Y; Kan R; Xiang Y; Mao B; Wang S; Li D; Yu X

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human cohort (correlation) + mouse (Angptl8-/- knockout, lifespan) + primary adipocyte/cell studies
studies.finding: Identifies ANGPTL8 as an endocrine driver of adipose-tissue aging: circulating ANGPTL8 tracked with biological age and mortality risk in a large human cohort, and genetic deletion of Angptl8 in mice extended lifespan and reduced senescence markers. Mechanistically, ANGPTL8 binds AKT2 and drives the AKT-mTOR-S6K axis to promote adipocyte senescence; blocking that axis abolished the pro-senescent effect.

studies.title: Continuous sensing of nutrients and growth factors by the mTORC1-TFEB axis
studies.authors: Sparta B; Albeck JG et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human MCF10A cells (live single-cell imaging, fluorescent TFEB fusions)
studies.finding: Live imaging of single MCF10A cells shows mTORC1-TFEB signalling adjusts continuously to amino acids and insulin, given alone, one after another or together; at physiological amino acid levels TFEB, AMPK and AKT activity fluctuate in step, and these graded changes track protein synthesis rate through a distributed set of mTORC1 effectors.

studies.title: Brucella suis vaccine strain 2 promotes intracellular proliferation by inducing M2 macrophage polarization and autophagy through PI3K/Akt/mTOR signalling.
studies.authors: Li H; Yang J; Xu T; Ji Z; Wang Zhenhai

studies.finding: Brucella suis vaccine strain 2 drives mixed M1/M2 macrophage polarisation and autophagic activation in BV2 cells; the M2 state and autophagy synergistically promote intracellular bacterial replication through PI3K/Akt/mTOR signalling.

studies.title: Corilagin attenuates osteoarthritis progression by coordinating NF-κB inhibition with PI3K/AKT/mTOR-associated autophagy restoration.
studies.authors: Zhou R; Li Jie; Chen S et al.

evidence.label: Animal model

studies.model_system: Mouse (DMM OA model); primary mouse chondrocytes
studies.finding: Corilagin restores chondrocyte autophagic flux and ECM synthesis by inhibiting PI3K/AKT/mTOR and NF-κB signalling, reducing cartilage erosion and OARSI scores in the mouse DMM osteoarthritis model.

studies.title: Impaired mTOR/SREBP1-Mediated Lipogenesis as a Mechanism of Hepatic Glycogen Accumulation in a Carnivorous Fish Model, Largemouth Bass (Micropterus salmoides)
studies.authors: Tao J; Chen S; Liu N; Gong Y; Zhang S; He J; Huang X; Chen N; Li S

In this model -- a carnivorous fish -- impairment of the axis is associated with hepatic glycogen overload mimicking glucose intolerance.

studies.finding: Topical pungenin accelerated hair regrowth in DHT-induced androgenetic alopecia mice, reducing type II 5α-reductase expression and modulating PI3K/AKT/FoxO/mTOR transcriptional signalling in hair follicle cells.

studies.title: mTORC1 inhibition upregulates CD20 and enhances anti-CD20 antibody efficacy in B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia
studies.authors: Dąbkowska A, Janowska M, Pastorczak A, Domka K, Nowicka Z, Urbanska Z, Zając W, Bugajewski M, Grzybowska J, Pruchniak P, Fidyt K, Fendler W, Taslim J, Crump NT, Ushmorov A, Patkowska E, Firczuk M

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure

studies.finding: mTORC1 inhibitors upregulate CD20 via the AKT-FOXO1 axis and promote B-lineage maturation in B-cell precursor ALL, enhancing the antitumor efficacy of anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies -- including in high-risk IKZF1-deleted disease -- providing a rationale for combining mTORC1 inhibition with CD20-directed immunotherapy.

studies.authors: Lassila P; Karpale M; Kummu O et al.

studies.authors: Zinzalla V; Hall MN et al.

studies.finding: mTORC2 is activated by direct association with the ribosome downstream of PI3K.

studies.title: Inferring feedback regulation from static snapshots of a single signal
studies.authors: Ginzberg M; Tan C; Patel N; Kafri R

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human/mammalian cultured cells (fixed-cell single-cell imaging, ergodic rate analysis)
studies.finding: Introduces AoF (Assay of Feedback), a perturbation-free single-cell imaging method that reconstructs how a signal CHANGES OVER TIME from fixed-cell snapshots, using DNA content and Geminin to order cells along the cell cycle. Applied to Akt phosphorylation, it uncovers a negative feedback loop that is active only in a narrow window at the G1/S transition; biochemistry points to mTORC1/S6K1-dependent inhibitory phosphorylation of IRS1 as the likely source, though the authors state this edge is not uniquely established. Directly relevant to the question of whether mTOR pathway activity is better described as a time-varying pattern than a fixed level.

studies.title: Feeding-Induced Muscle mTORC1 Signaling Regulates Postprandial Protein Synthesis and Endurance but Not Muscle Size
studies.authors: Lapp SC; Kalafut KC; Cissé MY; Tighanimine K; Rosenthal DM; Doxsey W; Hui S; Inouye KE; Morrow CE; Cormerais Y; Manning BD

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: SkM-TSC2-5A knock-in mice (AKT-phosphorylation-resistant TSC2, skeletal muscle-specific) vs SkM-TSC2-WT littermates, both sexes
studies.finding: Using a mouse model expressing an AKT-nonphosphorylatable TSC2 mutant specifically in skeletal muscle, the Manning lab genetically separated feeding-induced from contraction-induced mTORC1 activation. AKT-mediated TSC2 phosphorylation is required for feeding (but not contraction) to activate muscle mTORC1 and drive postprandial protein synthesis — yet mice lacking this feeding-induced signal have normal muscle mass and myofiber size, and instead show improved maximal endurance capacity with a modest rise in mitochondrial content. The finding dissociates mTORC1's role in postprandial anabolism from its role in maintaining steady-state muscle mass, and is a directly relevant data point for whether the pattern/source of mTORC1 activation (feeding vs. mechanical) — not just its average level — shapes downstream outcomes.

studies.title: Lysosomal mTORC2/PHLPP1/Akt regulate chaperone-mediated autophagy
studies.authors: Arias E; Koga H; Diaz A; Mocholi E; Patel B; Cuervo AM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse liver, rat liver, cell lines (NIH 3T3)
studies.finding: Extends the mTOR-autophagy relationship to a third form of autophagy that the Atlas otherwise does not cover, and reverses two of its usual terms. Here it is mTORC2, not mTORC1, that sits on the lysosomal membrane, and it inhibits chaperone-mediated autophagy through Akt, while the phosphatase PHLPP1 counteracts it; the balance controls assembly and disassembly of the translocation complex that pulls single proteins into the lysosome. Boundary: mechanism in cells and rodent liver; the claim that restoring this axis helps in ageing or disease is proposed, not tested here.

studies.title: Evidence for direct activation of mTORC2 kinase activity by phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate
studies.authors: Gan X; Wu D et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: PIP3 directly stimulates mTORC2 kinase activity, linking PI3K to mTORC2.

relations.mechanism: Akt phosphorylates PRAS40, which then gets sequestered away from mTORC1 - a second, parallel way insulin lifts a brake.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Akt tags PRAS40, which then gets pulled away from mTORC1 – a second way insulin releases a brake.

relations.mechanism: Akt phosphorylates TSC2, disabling the complex. Growth-factor signalling works by removing a brake, not by pressing an accelerator.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Akt tags TSC2 to disable it. Growth signals work by releasing a brake, not by pressing a gas pedal.
relations.boundary: In mouse liver, Akt phosphorylation of TSC2 is the main route by which insulin switches on mTORC1, but feeding activates hepatic mTORC1 without it; that response needs dietary protein instead (KAL2026). The biochemical mechanism itself was shown in cultured human cells (INO2002).

relations.mechanism: mTORC2 puts the second, activating phosphate on Akt (Ser473). This is the step rapamycin eventually breaks, and a major reason, in mice, that chronic rapamycin impairs glucose tolerance (LAM2012).
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC2 adds the final activating tag to Akt – the same step that long-term use of the drug rapamycin eventually disrupts. In mice, that disruption is a major reason long-term rapamycin raises blood sugar.
relations.context: S473 contribution to Akt output is substrate-dependent: some Akt substrates are strongly mTORC2-dependent, others barely.
relations.note: Bridge edge between the growth-factor route and the rapamycin route.

relations.mechanism: PIP3 pulls Akt to the membrane, where it gets phosphorylated and activated.
relations.mechanism_beginner: That lipid pulls Akt to the cell membrane, where it gets switched on.
relations.context: PIP3 recruits Akt; recruitment alone does not activate it. Full activation additionally needs PDK1 (T308) and mTORC2 (S473), so the strength of this link depends on the activity of both of those.

relations.mechanism: Akt phosphorylates FOXO transcription factors and excludes them from the nucleus. Rictor or mLST8 deletion abolishes signalling to Akt–FOXO while sparing S6K1.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Akt tags FOXO proteins and keeps them out of the nucleus; this specific link belongs to mTORC2, not mTORC1.
relations.context: This Akt output depends on mTORC2. Deleting rictor or mLST8 in mice removed Akt signalling to FOXO while S6K1 was spared (GUE2006), and SIN1, an essential mTORC2 subunit, controls Akt Ser473 phosphorylation and which substrates Akt reaches (JAC2006). The mTORC2-to-Akt step itself is the separate edge MTORC2-AKT.
relations.boundary: Mouse knockouts and cell lines; FOXO isoform contributions differ by tissue.
